messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the gpu-operator 1.8.0 rollout to eu-west we started seeing GPU pods stuck Pending. Scheduler is rejecting due to 'no GPUs' even though nodes show allocatable GPUs earlier today.
deploy-bot: gpu-operator v1.8.0 rollout finished for cluster: redwood-eu-west (40 nodes) :white_check_mark:
jamal: Can you paste the kubelet/device-plugin logs and `kubectl describe node` for an affected host?
mar ia: pasted two snippets below, one from `kubectl describe node gpu-eu-03` and one from kubelet: 
```
Non-terminated Pods:         (20 in total)
  Allocatable:
    nvidia.com/gpu:  0
    cpu:             32
    memory:          256Gi
Events:
  Warning  FailedAllocate  2m  kube-scheduler  failed to allocate resources: requested 1 nvidia.com/gpu, available 0
```
kubelet log snippet: 
```
I0223 14:12:01.123] device plugin: registered device plugin for nvidia
I0223 14:12:01.124] kubelet: advertise allocatable nvidia.com/gpu=0
I0223 14:12:01.125] driver-probe: waiting for kernel module ready
```
jamal: That `advertise allocatable nvidia.com/gpu=0` is the key. Looks like the device-plugin registered before the driver probe finished and advertised zero.
olga: I'm seeing this in dmesg on one node: 
```
[  10.234567] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[  10.234568] nvidia: probe of 0000:65:00.0 failed with error -22
```
andre: This matches a known race introduced by the operator's reorder of the driver-install and device-plugin DaemonSets. Device-plugin came up earlier on certain kernels and advertised zero GPUs. The scheduler caches that and pods stay Pending.
luis-oncall: Affected pool is eu-west-gpu-rt (preemptible, burstable). If we can't free these nodes, customers may hit capacity and we'll shift jobs to us-west which will blow monthly GPU cloud budget. Need quick mitigation.
jamal: Emergency mitigation: mark nodes with the tainted label so gpu pods don't schedule there and let autoscaler add replacement nodes in other pools? That buys time but costs money.
olga: Quick workaround that worked in staging: restart device-plugin after driver modules loaded. Command: `kubectl -n gpu-system rollout restart daemonset nvidia-device-plugin` — but we need to ensure driver daemonset finishes first.
sre-bot: Incident created: INF-2025-4321 "gpu-operator device-plugin advertise race in eu-west" — paging oncall.
maria: Can we target a rollback of the operator to 1.7.3 for eu-west only? That was stable.
andre: We have a canary process. Proposal: roll back gpu-operator on 4 nodes (canary), verify device-plugin advertises >0, then roll forward or rollback cluster-wide. I can prepare the manifest.
luis-oncall: I'm going to cordon/evict the worst offenders and restart device-plugin on those nodes. Will post exact node list in a sec.
jamal: Also worth noting: NCCL pods on some affected nodes reported errors about missing topology, so multi-gpu jobs might have been silently degraded before the Pending spike. Need to sweep for failed runs.
maria: Agree. Maria -> creating a quick eval query to find failed jobs in the last 30m and raising with CS.
andre: For the medium-term fix we should change the operator helm chart to set `driver.install.waitForModule=true` and reorder the device-plugin startup to `postStart` check for `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` before advertising. I'll open a PR.
olga: Patch idea looks good. Also add node annotation to indicate driver-version and a readiness probe for the device-plugin to re-advertise when driver appears.
jamal: OK action items: (1) canary rollback 4 nodes (andre), (2) cordon+evict+restart plugin for top 10 impacted nodes (luis-oncall/olga), (3) open PR to operator chart reordering (andre), (4) notify CS + cost impact calc (maria). I'll own rollout decision.
maria: Noted. Will ping @cs-team and attach temporary status page.
sre-bot: Update: rollback initiated in eu-west canary group by jamal at 14:28 UTC.
luis-oncall: First cordon+restart done on gpu-eu-03 — device-plugin now advertises `nvidia.com/gpu=8`, pods moved to Running for that node. Doing batch of 3 more.
maria: Thanks team. Will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
